history.dynasty: Merta Rathore chieftains (grandfather Rao Duda/Dudhoji; later contributions from Meera Bai and Jaimal)
history.period: 15th-16th century (original construction by Rao Dudhoji; ~400-year-old structure)
history.summary: CSV town corrected: this temple is at Merta City, Nagaur district - not in Nagaur town (Merta is ~80 km from Nagaur). Saint-poet Meera Bai (1498-1547), granddaughter of Rao Duda of Merta, worshipped here before her marriage into Mewar; the temple is dedicated to Charbhuja Nath (four-armed Vishnu/Krishna), the black murti of whom tradition says was revealed in the ground after a cobbler's cow miraculously milked onto the spot. Rao Dudhoji built the temple following a dream-vision of the deity; later contributions came from Meera Bai and Jaimal. Tradition holds Meera merged with the deity here. A monolithic statue of Meera Bai - carved by a sculptor who vowed to fast until it was finished - stands with eyes fixed on the deity. The complex also has an ancient Nagnecha Mata shrine and the Meera research institute/museum; a Meera memorial (smarak) stands nearby. Note: Meera was born at Kudki (Pali district), not at Merta - Merta was her grandfather's seat and childhood home. Do not confuse with the Charbhuja temple at Gadhbor (Rajsamand district), the better-known Charbhuja shrine.

name: Meera Bai Temple
town_description: Merta City is a historic town in Nagaur district, the former seat of the Merta Rathores (descendants of Rao Jodha of Jodhpur) and the childhood home of saint-poet Meera Bai. It is a well-known Krishna pilgrimage centre and a centre of Meera research.

travel.airport: Jodhpur Airport is the nearest major airport (~105-115 km); Jaipur International Airport is ~150-160 km away (distances approximate - verify).
travel.railway: Merta City has its own station; Merta Road Junction (~17 km) is the major railhead on the Jodhpur-Jaipur line.
travel.road: Well connected by road from Nagaur (~80 km), Jodhpur and Ajmer; the temple is on Meera Marg near the Central Bank in Merta.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; festival days (Janmashtami, Jhulotsava, Ekadashi bhajan evenings) are the most vibrant.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 04:30 am - 12:30 pm (TripHobo); evening hours not documented - verify before visiting.
